chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'By Allah, we indeed seek the world and love to attain it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'What do you love to do with it?' He said: 'I benefit myself and my family with it, maintain kinship with it, give in charity with it, perform Hajj, and perform Umrah.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not seeking the world; this is seeking the Hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between seeking the world and seeking the Hereafter according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines the concept of *Talab al-Dunya* (seeking the world) by distinguishing between mere accumulation and purposeful utilization. He clarifies that when wealth is employed for sustenance, family ties, charity, and worship, it becomes a means to attain the Hereafter, thereby transforming a worldly pursuit into an act of devotion. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the world is not inherently evil but serves as a tool for spiritual advancement when used in accordance with divine guidance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said,

‘A man said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! We tend to seek the world and we love to achieve it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is that which you love to do with it?’ He said, ‘Improve by it upon myself, and upon my family, and matain relationships with it, and give in charity with it, and perform Hajj and Umrah’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is not seeking the world. This is seeking the Hereafter’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from ‘Abd Allah ibn abu Ya’fur who has said the following:

“A man once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘We, by Allah, ask for the worldly things and we love to receive worldly gains.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What do you want to do with it?’ He replied, ‘I like to improve my own conditions, the conditions of my family, maintain good relations with others, give charity, perform Hajj and al-‘Umrah.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is not asking for worldly things. It is asking for success in the hereafter.’”
